title: Confidence ≠ correctness
summary: Distribution-derived confidence is not a guarantee about an individual domain assertion.

sections.label: Verified meaning
sections.text: TypeSafe’s confidence measure reflects the shape of the answer distribution. Treat calibration as something to evaluate over relevant examples, not a certificate attached to one result.

sections.label: Threshold practice
sections.text: Choice and Score confidence thresholds need task-specific evaluation; Noul does not return confidence. Tune routing separately for the exact question, primitive, language, and task. Do not multiply separate outputs as if their errors were independent.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: Routing thresholds achieve acceptable measured missed-error/false-alarm behavior. Two agreeing models remain two judgments, not independent source evidence.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended use: Evaluate confidence thresholds on the exact primitive, language and task before using them for routing.
Compare threshold decisions with independently reviewed labels.
Report missed errors and false alarms by language and difficult case subset.
Workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Existing examples, tenant availability, older product claims and comparative benefits were not revalidated by this mapping review.

catalog.applicability: Use this Jev example when you set or interpret Choice and Score confidence thresholds for routing. Evaluate calibration over relevant examples instead of treating one confidence value as a certificate attached to one result.
